obligations.behavior: issuing a credential for a human revokes any prior one in the same transaction; two concurrent issues leave exactly one active credential, and the replaced agent's IRC connection is closed
obligations.source_text: Every human (approved or guest) may bring exactly one personal agent; the agent connects over MCP, is authenticated through its human's email, and counts as that human (same tier, same permissions, no extra seat)

obligations.seam: agent connection receive path -> MCP read
obligations.behavior: a line from any sender other than the agent's human that DMs or @-addresses the agent is withheld; every delivered line carries an owner/not-owner mark taken from lens state
obligations.source_text: A human can talk with their own agent; no human can talk with another human's agent (user A can't reach user B's agent, user A can reach user A's agent)

obligations.behavior: join, send, read/history, channels, who, mesh, agents and live PRIVMSG dispatch each consult the grant check; an ungranted request emits no IRC line and returns a refusal
obligations.source_text: Channel permissions are enforced server-side in the lens Session for every path — join, send, read/history, channels listing, roster/who, raw /input — not only by hiding channels in the UI

obligations.behavior: an admin passes every channel check; a non-admin with no grant row fails every check (default-deny, never default-allow on a missing or unreadable grant)
obligations.source_text: Roles: admins have full access to every channel; for everyone else no grant means no channels (default-deny)

obligations.behavior: a read-level grant allows list/history/live lines and refuses every send verb; write/ask allows both
obligations.source_text: Two per-channel access levels: read, and write/ask

obligations.behavior: a guest principal always maps to the sandbox backend; an approved non-admin maps to the mesh, with no route to the sandbox guest view
obligations.source_text: Guests stay separate on the sandbox; approved (signed) users reach the real mesh, limited to their granted channels

obligations.behavior: an agent's grants are read from its human's current rows on every check; revoking the human's grant refuses the agent's next call
obligations.source_text: A personal agent can be wherever its owner is, with exactly its owner's permissions

obligations.behavior: a request without a valid, unexpired, unrevoked credential is refused before any tool runs; credentials are stored only as hashes
obligations.source_text: The single remote MCP endpoint (HTTP, not stdio) authenticates each agent with its own bearer credential: issued through its human's existing approval path (allowlist sign-in for approved users, email code for guests — per q5), stored hashed, bound to the human, revocable and expiring; the agent gets its own IRC connection and a nick visibly tied to its human

obligations.behavior: banning or deleting a human refuses and disconnects their agent and removes its credential rows
obligations.source_text: The agent is accounted as its human everywhere the human is: it takes no extra guest seat, is checked against is_banned(email, ip), its flags use the human's key, idle sign-off and deletion (delete_guest_inputs, delete_sessions_for_email) and the retention sweep cover it

obligations.behavior: a TCP connect to the mesh IRC port from a non-allowed source is refused; the lens, mesh agents and links still connect
obligations.source_text: The mesh IRCd accepts connections only from the lens, the mesh's own agents and its federation links — restricting it is part of this feature, because the IRCd has no access control and lens-side grants are otherwise bypassable

obligations.behavior: one endpoint serves all tiers; the scope comes only from the credential's bound human, never from request parameters
obligations.source_text: One MCP endpoint for all tiers (admin, approved, guest), reached through the lens's public host; for now an agent is approved the same way a human is today

obligations.seam: admin-only routes (sandbox enter, owner metrics, residents)
obligations.behavior: a non-admin approved user or any agent gets 403
obligations.source_text: Admin-only surfaces: the sandbox 'guest view' toggle (which joins every guest's private room), the owner metrics page and the residents page are available to admins only — never to non-admin approved users or any agent

obligations.behavior: a DM to the agent from a raw IRC client that bypasses the lens is withheld from MCP reads
obligations.source_text: Owner-only filtering runs on the receive side of the agent's lens-held IRC connection, so it covers every sender — other lens users, federated peers, and any client that reached the IRCd directly

obligations.behavior: no tool call runs without a resolved human identity; the dev-only identity-less tools path is never reachable from the endpoint
obligations.source_text: The MCP endpoint does not reuse the identity-less tools.py path (fixed dev nick, dev-mode only); every MCP tool call carries its credential's human and passes the same grant check as the web Session

obligations.behavior: agent sends go through the same allowlist, rate limit, input log and flag path as the human's web input
obligations.source_text: An agent's sends pass the same gates as its human's: the guest command allowlist, the per-human rate limit, the input log and the flag path; one agent cannot exhaust a shared resident's answer capacity

obligations.behavior: each request re-checks the human is still approved / not banned / not deleted
obligations.source_text: Every agent request re-checks its human's current status (still approved, not banned, not deleted), so removing an approved user or banning a guest cuts off their agent on its next request

obligations.behavior: the kill switch refuses every agent call; disabling permissions refuses non-admins the mesh instead of granting all of it
obligations.source_text: Rollback fails closed: a single switch disables the MCP endpoint and blocks all agent credentials, and turning the permissions feature off never restores full mesh access to non-admin approved users

obligations.behavior: a non-admin approved user, a guest or any agent calling these routes gets 403; an invite never grants access before the invited user completes sign-in
obligations.source_text: Admins add and invite non-admin approved users, and manage their grants, from within the app

obligations.behavior: with no live admin extension the agent's connection closes in the same reap as its human; with one it stays until the extension's end time, then follows the normal rule
obligations.source_text: A guest's agent is disconnected when its human is signed off for idleness, unless an admin has approved that agent to stay for a set period of n hours (chosen by the admin), after which the normal rule applies again

obligations.behavior: enabling permissions with zero admins in the store is refused with a hint; after migration the previously approved users are admins
obligations.source_text: The migration marks currently approved users as admins (today only the operator); the feature refuses to enable while zero admins exist

obligations.behavior: the migration imports the config allowlist exactly once (re-running it imports nothing new) and afterwards the config list is never read for access
obligations.source_text: Approved users and admin flags live in the lens store; the migration imports the existing config allowlist once and the config list is then retired
